title: Non-Invasive Neurovascular Assessment of symptoms in Persistent Post-Concussion Syndrome
summary:
After a mild head injury, such as a concussion, some people experience long-lasting symptoms. These can last for weeks to months and include headaches, dizziness, vision problems, difficulty concentrating, mood swings, or severe fatigue. These symptoms can significantly impact daily life.

Concussions are often considered harmless since there are no visible injuries on the outside. Additionally, there are no standardized tests or targeted treatments available, as recovery varies greatly among individuals. However, recent studies suggest that tiny blood vessels in the brain and their function may be impaired.

In our study, we aim to investigate patients aged 18 to 65 years with persistent symptoms following a concussion. We use a painless, non-invasive ultrasound method to measure the responsiveness of blood vessels in the brain. The goal is to better understand which symptoms are linked to these changes and, in the long term, improve the treatment of concussions.

interventions.name: Patients with PPCS up to a maximum of 6 months post-concussion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient Cohort: 
• Medically diagnosed concussion within the last 12 months
• Post-Concussion Syndrome with 3 typical symptoms (e.g. headaches, dizziness, fatigue, irritability, sleep disturbances, sensitivity to light/sound, memory/concentration problems)
• Age 18 – 65 years
• Willingness to participate and comply with study protocols

Healthy Controls: 
• Age 18 – 65 years
• No prior diagnosed concussion
• Willingness to participate and comply with study protocols
Exclusion criteria:
Patients and study participants:
• Relevant cerebrovascular diseases (including myocardial infarction, heart failure)
• Cerebrovascular stenosis
• Lack of consent capacity
